subject: Marketplace renewal — split acceptance & onboarding checkpoints
messages:
From: Kara Lin <kara.lin@blueharbor.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Blue Harbor Procurement <procurement@blueharbor.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Marketplace renewal: alignment on acceptance waves and onboarding checkpoints

Hi Dylan,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. We're ready to move forward with the 12-month commit, but procurement needs a targeted acceptance and onboarding schedule before we can sign the private offer on the AWS Marketplace. Two asks from our side: 

1) Split acceptance window: we need the commitment divided into an initial acceptance (60% capacity) and a follow-up acceptance (40%) 90 days later so our integration team can stage traffic.
2) Evidence bundle: SOC2 evidence, a short SOW that maps services to the Marketplace SKUs, and a single DocuSign link to route to our procurement approver.

Can you confirm Redwood can produce those artifacts and whether you can support a staggered invoicing cadence? Our CFO would also like a short note on credits if we exit early within the first 6 months.

Appreciate a concise plan and who on your side owns each deliverable.

Best,
Kara
Kara Lin
Procurement Manager, Blue Harbor Systems
[Attachment: BHS_Renewal_Request.pdf (application/pdf)]

Subject: Re: Marketplace renewal: alignment on acceptance waves and onboarding checkpoints

Hi Kara — thanks for the clear asks. Short answer: yes, we can support the split acceptance, the evidence bundle, and a staged invoicing plan. High-level plan below and owners.

Plan (deliverables + owner + ETA):
- Acceptance wave plan (document): Dylan Brooks — today EOD PT. Will map 60/40 split and exact dates for the 90-day follow-up.
- Evidence bundle (SOC2 summary + SOW + Marketplace SKU map): Marissa Cole (Legal/Onboarding) — draft by Thu 20 Aug.
- DocuSign private offer routing (single link to procurement approver): Ben Carter (Sales Ops) — will generate and share link by Thu 20 Aug.
- Invoicing cadence & early-exit credit note: Ben Carter + Finance — initial proposal by Fri 21 Aug.

Attachments I'm sending: BHS_SOW_v2.pdf (draft SOW that ties our service tiers to AWS SKUs) and a quick wave-plan spreadsheet (redwood-acceptance-waveplan.xlsx).

Next steps: if this looks good, I'll update our Marketplace PO and have Ben create the DocuSign envelope for your approver. If procurement needs a specific invoice schedule (monthly/tranche), flag the desired cadence in your reply.

Thanks,
Dylan

Procurement preference: tranche invoicing (60% on initial acceptance, 40% on follow-up). Early-exit: our legal wants a standard 30% credit if we terminate within months 1–6 (we can negotiate exact language in redlines).

Please route the DocuSign to alice.mellor@blueharbor.com (Finance approver) and include a one-page acceptance checklist that our integration lead can validate.

I'll hold for Ben's DocuSign link and Marissa's evidence package.

Best,
Kara
